title: Adic evaluation of completed monoid algebras and congruence of evaluations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak a$ a finitely generated ideal of $R$. Let $P$ be a finitely generated commutative additive monoid which is sharp, meaning that its only invertible element is $0$. Write $R[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}Rz^p$, with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$, put $\mathfrak b=(\mathfrak a,z^p:p\ne0)$, and put $B=\varprojlim_n R[P]/\mathfrak b^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J$ an ideal, and suppose that $A$ is $J$-adically complete and separated [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $\alpha:R\to A$ be a ring homomorphism with $\alpha(\mathfrak a)\subseteq J$. For every homomorphism $a:(P,+)\to(A,\cdot)$ with $a(0)=1$ and $a(p)\in J$ for $p\ne0$, there is a unique continuous ring homomorphism $E_a:B\to A$ which restricts to $\alpha$ on $R$ and sends $z^p$ to $a(p)$. It satisfies $E_a(\mathfrak b^nB)\subseteq J^n$ for every $n\ge0$. If $a,b$ are two such monoid homomorphisms, $p_1,\ldots,p_h$ are nonzero generators of $P$, and $a(p_i)-b(p_i)\in J^r$ for every $i$, where $r\ge1$, then $E_a(f)-E_b(f)\in J^r$ for every $f\in B$.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, finite-level completion kernels; agent-supplied monoid evaluation and congruence refinement of this inverse-limit construction, for ILO VI 2.3.

proof.text: Put $S=R[P]$ and let $\iota:S\to B$ be the canonical map. Choose generators $u_1,\ldots,u_t$ of $\mathfrak a$ and a finite generating list $q_1,\ldots,q_h$ of $P$ with its zero entries removed. Every nonzero $p\in P$ has an expression as a nonempty sum of these $q_i$, so $z^p$ is a multiple of some $z^{q_i}$. Consequently $\mathfrak b=(u_1,\ldots,u_t,z^{q_1},\ldots,z^{q_h})$ is finitely generated. For $P=\{0\}$ take the empty list.

source.place: Agent argument: finite generation needed for Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] to the commutative ring $S$ and its finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak b$. For every $n\ge1$ the coordinate projection $\pi_n:B\to S/\mathfrak b^n$ has kernel $\mathfrak b^nB$ and satisfies $\pi_n\iota(g)=g\bmod\mathfrak b^n$. In particular, for each $f\in B$ choose a representative $g_n\in S$ of $\pi_n(f)$; then $f-\iota(g_n)\in\mathfrak b^nB$. Thus the coordinate-kernel neighborhoods and the $(\mathfrak bB)$-adic neighborhoods coincide, since $(\mathfrak bB)^n=\mathfrak b^nB$ by expanding products of generators.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated (2) and final paragraph, specialized to M = S; agent spelling out polynomial representatives.

proof.text: Define $e_a:S\to A$ by the finite sum $e_a(\sum_p c_pz^p)=\sum_p\alpha(c_p)a(p)$. Addition and the unit are preserved since $a(0)=1$. For multiplication, expanding the two finite supports gives $\sum_{p,q}\alpha(c_p d_q)a(p+q)=\sum_{p,q}\alpha(c_p)\alpha(d_q)a(p)a(q)$, which is the product of the two evaluations. This uses only $a(p+q)=a(p)a(q)$, so no cancellation or integrality of $P$ is assumed. The generators of $\mathfrak b$ go into $J$; expressing elements of $\mathfrak b^n$ as finite sums of multiples of products of $n$ generators proves $e_a(\mathfrak b^n)\subseteq J^n$ for every $n\ge0$.

source.place: Agent finite-sum computation using the monoid-algebra operations written in the item.

proof.text: The previous containment makes $\bar e_{a,n}:S/\mathfrak b^n\to A/J^n$, $[g]\mapsto[e_a(g)]$, a well-defined ring map. For $m\le n$, reducing this formula to $A/J^m$ equals first reducing $[g]$ to $S/\mathfrak b^m$ and then applying $\bar e_{a,m}$. Hence $f\mapsto(\bar e_{a,n}(\pi_n(f)))_n$ takes values in $\varprojlim_n A/J^n$ and is a ring map: the compatibility and all ring operations are checked coordinatewise [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Compose it with the inverse of the canonical ring isomorphism $A\to\varprojlim_n A/J^n$ supplied by the definition of completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. The resulting ring map $E_a:B\to A$ satisfies $E_a(f)\bmod J^n=\bar e_{a,n}(\pi_n(f))$. Substituting $f=\iota(g)$ shows $E_a\iota=e_a$, since their residues agree for all $n$ and $A$ is separated. This gives the required values on $R$ and on every $z^p$.

source.place: Definition Tag 0317, definition-complete, and section-completion: agent coordinatewise construction of the evaluation map.

proof.text: An element of $\mathfrak b^nB$ is a finite sum $\sum_j\iota(v_j)f_j$ with $v_j\in\mathfrak b^n$ and $f_j\in B$. Applying $E_a$ gives $\sum_j e_a(v_j)E_a(f_j)\in J^n$. This proves the claimed filtration bound, including $n=0$, where it is simply $E_a(B)\subseteq A$. For every $n$, therefore, the preimage of $J^n$ contains the open ideal $\mathfrak b^nB$ from step 2. Translation by any $f\in B$ gives continuity at $f$ for the adic topologies.

source.place: Agent finite ideal-generator calculation; the coordinate-kernel topology is identified in step 2.

proof.text: Let $F:B\to A$ be any continuous ring map with the specified coefficient and monomial values. On a finite sum in $S$ those values give $F\iota=e_a$. The same finite ideal-generator calculation as in step 5 yields $F(\mathfrak b^nB)\subseteq J^n$. For $f\in B$ use the representative $g_n$ of step 2: both $F(f)$ and $E_a(f)$ equal $e_a(g_n)$ modulo $J^n$. Thus $F(f)-E_a(f)\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}J^n=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], giving uniqueness. No extra density theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated (2), and Definition Tag 0317; agent uniqueness argument with finite-level representatives.

proof.text: Now let $a,b$ satisfy the stated congruences on $p_1,\ldots,p_h$. For any $p$, choose an expression $p=p_{i_1}+\cdots+p_{i_k}$; when $p=0$ use the empty expression. Set $x_j=a(p_{i_j})$ and $y_j=b(p_{i_j})$. The finite identity $\prod_{j=1}^k x_j-\prod_{j=1}^k y_j=\sum_{j=1}^k(x_j-y_j)(\prod_{l<j}x_l)(\prod_{l>j}y_l)$ shows $a(p)-b(p)\in J^r$, with zero difference for the empty product. Applying the finite-sum formula of step 3 gives $e_a(g)-e_b(g)\in J^r$ for every $g\in S$. For $f\in B$ choose $g_r$ as in step 2 using [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Step 5 for each evaluation sends $f-\iota(g_r)\in\mathfrak b^rB$ into $J^r$. Therefore $E_a(f)-E_b(f)=E_a(f-\iota(g_r))+(e_a(g_r)-e_b(g_r))-E_b(f-\iota(g_r))\in J^r$. This establishes the congruence without taking a closure of $J^r$.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated (2), for the representative; agent telescoping-product argument for congruence.

The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live node, which is still unsplit. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and every step is under 900 characters. The statement is true and no hypothesis was weakened: R is arbitrary, 𝔞 is finitely generated, J is arbitrary and A is J-complete. Sharpness is unused and harmless, since an invertible p would give 1 ∈ J and so A=0. Step 1: 𝔟 is finitely generated because every z^p with p≠0 is a multiple of some z^{q_i}; P={0} is covered. Step 2: the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power (pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval, 05GG(2)) gives ker π_n = 𝔟^nB and the representatives g_n, and (𝔟B)^n = 𝔟^nB is elementary. Step 3: e_a is a ring map by a finite double sum using only a(p+q)=a(p)a(q), and e_a(𝔟^n) ⊆ J^n. Step 4: E_a is the inverse of A ≅ lim A/J^n composed with the compatible maps ē_{a,n}π_n, which uses exactly what the two definition leaves state, and E_aι = e_a. Step 5: elements of 𝔟^nB are Σι(v_j)f_j, so E_a(𝔟^nB) ⊆ J^n, and continuity follows from cosets. Step 6: uniqueness through g_n and ⋂J^n = 0; it does not even need continuity of F. Step 7: the telescoping product identity gives a(p)−b(p) ∈ J^r, then e_a−e_b on S, then the result for f via g_r, with no closure of J^r.
